incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: streaming-tail latency spike detected in eu-west-1. p95 1.2s -> 5.3s, p99 6.7s -> 10.9s. Affects SSE/WebSocket streaming clients, increased chunking delays. On-call: @oncall-1 alerted.
alice: Acknowledged. I'm grabbing traces. Which services show errors?
bryan: Load balancer / proxy (stream-proxy-eu) showing high write latency and many 504s to clients. Backend model infra seems OK. Client slow consumers piling up.
oncall-1: I'm on it. Putting temporary buffer-size bump and restarting streaming proxy pods in eu cluster. Will also enable keepalive probes. tl;dr: trying to clear blocked sockets.
carla: Support: customer X reporting truncated streams and reconnect storms. They're hitting us with long-lived streams. Rate limiting could hurt them, need to coordinate.
alice: Dumped tcp backlog + netstat: lots of connections in CLOSE_WAIT and high rmem usage. Also seeing 'EPIPE' in proxy logs around chunk write. Pasted snippet:
```
2026-03-15T10:12:03Z stream-proxy-eu write to socket failed: EPIPE (broken pipe)
2026-03-15T10:12:05Z client 10.2.4.55 slow consumer: write timeout 120s
```
bryan: Metric panels: socket_write_latency.p95 = 5200ms, socket_write_latency.p99 = 10900ms. Connection churn increased 3x. Proxy GC cycles low, CPU ok. Could be head-of-line blocking due to single-threaded writer.
sre-mgr: If proxy is single-threaded per connection, heavy slow consumers can stall others. We should enable per-connection write buffer limit and backpressure drop policy for >30s stalls. Also consider scaling stream-proxy-eu by +3 pods.
oncall-1: Scaling +3 started (k8s rollout). Applying buffer limits via configmap: stream_proxy.write_buffer_max=256KB, stream_proxy.drop_on_stall=true, stall_timeout_ms=30000. Rolling restart in progress.
support-bot: PD incident created: INC-65238. Customer impact: degraded streaming for ~12% of connections in EU, intermittent reconnects. Notified CSMs.
carla: Customer X willing to accept temporary degraded throughput if it stabilizes. Please keep me posted so I can update them.
alice: After changes, p95 dropped to 1.3s, p99 4.8s. Connection counts normalized. No more EPIPE spikes in last 2min. Preliminary root cause: long-lived slow-consumer connections and proxy write buffer growth coupled with socket write syscall blocking.
bryan: We also found a subtle bug in proxy's chunk flush logic when client window is 0: it retries writes in tight loop instead of yielding, causing head-of-line blocking across multiplexed worker. Patch ready: PR #8921 with yield/yield_backoff.
oncall-1: Handing off monitoring and remediation to next oncall (scheduled). Next oncall: @alice (taking next shift). Leaving playbook steps in INC-65238: 1) scale proxies, 2) apply buffer/drop config, 3) monitor p95/p99 and connection churn, 4) if persists, reroute EU clients to eu-n2 (fallback region) via rr-policy.
sre-mgr: Post-mortem required. Action items: (a) apply permanent write buffer defaults, (b) backport chunk flush patch to stable-1.x, (c) add unit test for slow-consumer path, (d) update runbook with threshold numbers. Owner assignments: bryan->PR, alice->runbook+metrics, carla->customer comms.
incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident acknowledged. Status: mitigated (partial). Keeping the thread open. If any regressions or re-escalation, react with :rotating_light:.
